newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-DEAD BOXER'S MOTHER OPPOSES BAN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-DEAD BOXER'S MOTHER OPPOSES BAN.

text.p: The mother of middleweight boxer Fabrizio De Chiara, who fell into a coma and died after an Italian title fight, said on Tuesday that she was against calls to ban the sport.
"When this sort of thing happened before, Fabrizio never said let's abolish boxing. If he thought like that he would never have stepped in the ring," the man's mother Clara told TG5 television news.
"I would be going against my son," she said when asked why she did not want the sport banned. "Even if he's dead, he did what he did of his own free will."
Magistrates in the central town of Carrara, near where the fight took place, have opened an enquiry into the death, which has led to renewed calls in Italy to outlaw boxing.

Saturday's fight was stopped mid-way through the 12th and final round after opponent Vincenzo Imparato landed two sharp blows to De Chiara's head followed by one to the stomach, knocking him to the ground.

The referee ended the fight and the shaven-headed De Chiara, 25, made it back to his corner before collapsing. He was immediately taken to hospital, but died following two operations to remove blood that was putting pressure on his brain.
His organs were donated for transplants.
De Chiara's mother said her son had been a fit man.
"Nobody goes into the ring to lose. My son was stubborn and proud and he would never have decided to throw in the towel of his own accord," she said.
"It turned out the way it did and that's the end of it," she said.
